activity.overview: Use random samples to estimate facts about a population, and describe how much estimates can vary.

problems.prompt: In a random sample of 80 students from a school of 720, 24 students walk to school. Estimate how many students in the school walk to school.

Three random samples of 50 voters were asked about a plan for a new park. In the samples, 28, 31 and 25 voters supported the plan. Estimate the percent of all voters who support the plan, and describe how much the samples vary.
A biologist catches and tags 60 fish in a lake, then releases them. Later she catches 100 fish, and 12 of them are tagged. Estimate the number of fish in the lake.

A random sample of 25 seventh graders reported a mean of 32 minutes of reading per day. Predict the mean reading time for all seventh graders in the school. Would a random sample of 5 students give a more reliable or less reliable prediction? Explain.
In a random sample of 40 students from a school of 400, 18 prefer a later start time. Estimate how many students in the school prefer a later start. Is your estimate certain to be exact? Explain.

activity.subject: mathematics
activity.title: Making Inferences from Samples
